root_cause.text: io_uring legacy buffer recycling in `io_kbuf_recycle_legacy()` reused a previously selected `req->kbuf` without revalidating that its `io_buffer_list` still existed and was still a legacy list, allowing a stale/changed buffer-list state after an io-wq gap.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says “There’s a gap between when the buffer was grabbed and when it potentially gets recycled” and that “The legacy recycling is missing checking if the buffer_list still exists, and if it’s of the correct type”; the patch adds `if (bl && !(bl->flags & IOBL_BUF_RING)) ... else { kfree(buf); }` before re-adding the buffer to `bl->buf_list`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly says “There’s a gap between when the buffer was grabbed and when it potentially gets recycled” and that “The legacy recycling is missing checking if the buffer_list still exists, and if it’s of the correct type”; the patch adds `if (bl && !(bl->flags & IOBL_BUF_RING)) ... else { kfree(buf); }` before re-adding the buffer to `bl->buf_list`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix legacy buffer recycling to drop and free buffers when their list was removed or upgraded to a ring buffer during in-flight execution, and clear the request's buffer pointer afterward.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the existing buffer recycle logic in a conditional that checks whether the buffer list lookup returned a non-NULL list and that the list is not ring-based (`bl && !(bl->flags & IOBL_BUF_RING)`). If that condition passes, it keeps the previous behavior of adding the buffer back to `bl->buf_list` and incrementing `bl->nbufs`; otherwise it frees the buffer with `kfree(buf)`. It also adds `req->kbuf = NULL` after clearing `REQ_F_BUFFER_SELECTED`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents a legacy buffer from being reinserted into an invalid or incompatible buffer list when the list was removed or converted to a ring-based buffer list while the request was still executing in io-wq. In those cases the buffer is discarded instead of being linked into the wrong structure, avoiding stale-pointer or list corruption issues, and clearing `req->kbuf` ensures the request no longer retains a dangling reference after recycle handling.

grouping_result.intent: Fix legacy buffer recycling to drop and free buffers when their list was removed or upgraded to a ring buffer during in-flight execution, and clear the request's buffer pointer afterward.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by revalidating legacy buffer-list state during recycling, freeing/dropping buffers if the list was removed or converted to a ring buffer, and clearing req->kbuf to avoid reusing stale buffer state after an io-wq gap.

candidates.rationale: This fetches the buffer list by bgid but, before the fix, its result was used without validating that the list still existed and was still a legacy buffer list. That missing revalidation is the core root cause.
This re-inserts the recycled buffer into whatever list pointer was returned, embodying the unsafe reuse of req->kbuf after state may have changed during the io-wq gap.
This updates the buffer count on the unvalidated buffer list, further reflecting the stale/changed-list misuse once req->kbuf was recycled without checking list validity/type.

This is the starting point of reusing a previously selected request buffer. The vulnerability stems from reusing this saved pointer across an execution gap without ensuring its originating list state remained valid.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the unsafe reinsertion of a recycled legacy buffer into a buffer list obtained after an io-wq gap, without first ensuring the list still exists and is still a legacy list. It directly manifests the stale/changed buffer-list reuse described in the root cause.
This retrieves the buffer list by bgid, but in the vulnerable code path the returned list was not revalidated to confirm it still existed and was still a legacy buffer list before reuse of req->kbuf.
This mutates metadata of the unvalidated buffer list after stale buffer recycling, contributing to the misuse of a removed or changed buffer-list state.
This reuses the previously selected request buffer across the execution gap. That saved pointer became unsafe to recycle without revalidating the associated buffer-list state.
